supplement.summary: 〜ずにはおかない declares that a force will not let things end without the verb happening. With causative or emotive verbs, the subject is often a thing whose power inevitably affects people: 聴く人を感動させずにはおかない = it cannot fail to move listeners. With a personal subject it voices fierce determination: 謝らせずにはおかない = I won't rest until I make him apologize. It is emphatic, formal, and written in flavor; する becomes せずにはおかない.

pitfalls: Don't confuse it with ずにはいられない, which is the speaker's own uncontrollable urge; ずにはおかない is an external force or resolve that will inevitably bring the action about.
In the 'inevitable effect' use the verb is typically causative (感動させる, 考えさせる) and the subject is often a work, event, or statement.
